Lemma. Practice staff-level interviews, out loud.
Lemma is a practice room for system design and coding interviews. One streak across both tracks, and everything stays on your Mac.
Pick a question and answer it out loud, one section at a time, through a five-part framework. Your speech is transcribed locally, and you can edit the transcript before it is graded.
Sketch the architecture as you talk. The grader reads your diagram too.
Then comes the report. Your answer is graded against a researched answer key, with a level, a hiring signal, and ten dimensions.
Every section shows the evidence, the gaps, and a drill for next time.
Gaps become explainer articles, grouped by design problem.
And progress tracks the gaps that keep coming back, across every session.
A roadmap of one hundred and sixty problems in Java. Every test suite is checked against an independent brute force before you ever see it.
Write real Java, with completion and live errors from the language server.
Then a staff-level review reads your code, not just your test results.
